prompt_md: 100 coins lie on a table, 10 of them heads up. Blindfolded, you must split them into two piles with equal heads; you may flip coins. How many go in the smaller pile?
prompt_short: 100 coins, 10 heads, blindfolded: equal-heads piles. Smaller pile size?
hint_md: Slide some coins aside, then flip every one of them.
explain_intuition_md: Two piles of 50 have no reason to match. Instead, slide any 10 coins aside and flip every one of them. If h of those 10 were heads, the big pile has 10 - h heads, and after flipping, the small pile has exactly 10 - h heads too.
explain_math_md: Small pile: $h$ heads before flipping, $10 - h$ after. Big pile: $10 - h$ heads. A pile of size $k$ works only when $k - h = 10 - h$, so $k = 10$.
